speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) to what extent are the textbooks and curriculums in primary and secondary schools adjusted to align with our goal of de-emphasising the outcome focus on academic scores and emphasising more on broad-based learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Our holistic education equips our students with a broad range of competencies needed for life and work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Besides the cognitive aspect, we also focus on the aesthetic, moral, physical and social domains.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: We ensure our students gain strong fundamentals in literacy and numeracy, as well as develop good values and their social and emotional competencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: These essential areas form the bedrock our students are able to draw from for their continual and lifelong learning beyond school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: To bring about engaged learners, teachers design lessons that use different pedagogies to help students develop a strong mastery of the discipline, appreciate the relevance of their learning and then apply it in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: It is regularly reviewed to ensure that the learning outcomes remain appropriate for our students and are responsive to future needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: Our teachers use a wide range of teaching resources to ensure that students learn from different modalities and immerse them in varied experiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: They also participate in outdoor learning and are given the chance to apply their knowledge in authentic situations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: At times, they need to draw on technology to synthesise concepts in new contexts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: For example, in our Science textbooks, students learn about the lives of scientists and the passion and perseverance they demonstrate in pushing the frontiers of scientific knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: The youngsters also get to appreciate and discuss the impact of science and technology on the environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: In Geography, students go on field trips to experience how theoretical concepts come alive.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: While I understand the importance of fundamentals and MOE is trying to develop a holistic approach for the students, the question that a lot of parents have is: are we doing too much and too early?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Even the parents have difficulties following the methodologies to teach their own children.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, do we need to break that cycle in order to help the students, or are we teaching them too much?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to reassure Miss Chan that in reviewing and adjusting our curriculum, MOE is always mindful of the support that our students need for their learning journey, and that different students have different needs and varied abilities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOE works with teachers, Heads of Departments (HODs), and school leaders.
